:::{.proof}
Let $x^* \in A$.
By @def-argmax, $x^*$ is in the [argmax](#def-argmax) of $c\,g$
[if and only if](proof-writing.qmd#def-iff)
$c\,g(a) \le c\,g(x^*)$ for every $a \in A$.

Suppose $g(a) \le g(x^*)$.
If $g(a) = g(x^*)$, then $c\,g(a) = c\,g(x^*)$.
If $g(a) < g(x^*)$, then $c\,g(a) < c\,g(x^*)$ by @thm-mult-ineq.
Either way, $c\,g(a) \le c\,g(x^*)$.

Conversely, suppose $c\,g(a) \le c\,g(x^*)$.
Since $1/c > 0$ and $(1/c)\,(c\,g) = g$,
the same reasoning applied to the [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-function) $c\,g$ and the multiple $1/c$ gives $g(a) \le g(x^*)$.

So $c\,g(a) \le c\,g(x^*)$ for every $a \in A$ if and only if $g(a) \le g(x^*)$ for every $a \in A$.
Hence $x^*$ is in the argmax of $c\,g$ exactly when it is in the argmax of $g$.
:::
